caseno: Criminal Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 282 of 2004
lawyer:
Md Rafiqul  Islam Mia, Advocate, instructed by Md Nawab Ali, Advocate-on-Record—For the Petitioner. 
AJ Mohammad Ali, Attorney-General, instructed by Zahirul Islam, Advocate-on-Record— For the Respondent.
parties:
Kamal Uddin ------ Petitioner
Vs.
State represented by the DC, Comilla ------ Respondent
full_judgment:
Amirul Kabir Chowdhury J: Accused-petitioner Kamal Uddin seeks leave to appeal against the judgment and order dated 8-8-2004 passed by a Division Bench of the High Court Division in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 3446 of 2003 discharging the Rule. 

 2. The facts as stated in the petition, in brief, are that one Enamul Haque lodged an ejahar on 8-3-2001 with Muradnagar Police Station stating, inter alia, that he along with Mizan Mia and Ayub Ali (cited as witness Nos.1 and 5 in FIR) while going to the bus terminal and came near the house of the accused-petitioner they met accused Hossain to whom the aforesaid Ayub Ali demanded his dues of Taka 1500 and then the accused became enraged and by his order the accused-petitioner Kamal Uddin and other accused surrounded him and assaulted the victim causing injuries and the victim was taken to Debiddar Thana Health Complex where he was declared dead and on the basis of aforesaid ejhar, Muradnagar PS Case No. 4 dated 8-3-2001 was started against the accused-petitioner and others under sections 302/34 of the Penal Code and the case after being investigated charge-sheet No. 19 dated 27-3-2001 was submitted against two accused while final report was submitted against the rest including the petitioner and that the informant filed naraji petition against the said final report and also filed an application to the Government for further investigation of the case and the learned Magistrate directed for further investigation and Mr Nurul Amin, Assistant Superintendent of Police, CID held further investigation and thereafter submitted supplementary charge-sheet No. 19 dated 3-12-2001 under sections 302/114/34 of the Penal Code implicating the accused petitioner and the supplementary charge sheet was accepted by the learned Magistrate who took cognisance against the accused-petitioner along with other accused and the case has been sent for trial before the learned Sessions Judge, Comilla where it has been registered as Sessions Case No. 365 of 2002 and the case has been transferred to the 4th Court of the learned Additional Sessions Judge for trial and the learned Additional Sessions Judge after hearing both the parties framed charge against the accused-petitioner and others under sections 302/34 of the Penal Code. 

 3. The accused petitioner thereafter moved the High Court Division in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 3446 of 2003 under sections 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure and the High Court Division after hearing the parties discharged the Rule as mentioned above. 

 5. Mr Md Rafiqul Islam Mia, learned Advocate appearing for the accused-petitioner, submits, inter alia, that the High Court Division committed error in failing to consider that the learned Magistrate, without considering the naraji petition filed by the informant against the final report keeping the same with the record, directed further investigation of the case and thereby committed error. 

 6. Mr A J Mohammad Ali, learned Attorney-General, on behalf of the State, opposes the petition contending, inter alia, that after proper investigation by an Assistant Superintendent of Police, supplementary charge-sheet has been submitted against the accused-petitioner on prima face materials and the trial Court after hearing the parties in the facts and circumstances of the case and materials on record framed charge against the accused petitioner and the High Court Division did not commit any error in discharging the Rule as the principles for quashing are not attracted in the facts and circumstances of the present case. 

 13. The aforesaid provision of law envisages that nothing in the section shall preclude further investigation in respect of an offence after a report under sub-section (1) of section 173 of the Code of Criminal Procedure (i.e. a charge-sheet or final report as the case may be) has been forwarded to the learned Magistrate by any investigating agency.
